target: Te quiero mucho.
english: I love you very much.
tip: 'Te quiero' is literally 'I want you' – yet it's the everyday 'I love you' for family and partners. Te amo is heavier, saved for deep romance.

target: Estamos a veinte de marzo.
english: It is March twentieth.
tip: "Estamos a veinte de marzo" is literally "we are at March 20th" – Spanish states today's date with estar a, with "we" as the subject.

target: Se me rompieron las gafas.
english: My glasses broke.
tip: The 'se + indirect object' pattern expresses unplanned events: 'se me olvidó' = it slipped my mind (lit. it forgot itself on me).

target: Son las cinco menos cuarto.
english: It's a quarter to five.
tip: Spanish tells time by subtraction: 'las cinco menos cuarto' = five MINUS a quarter. Past half past, count down from the coming hour.

target: Compré los billetes por internet.
english: I bought the tickets online.
tip: "Por internet" – "por" indicates the means/medium through which something is done.

target: Nos contó una historia increíble.
english: He told us an incredible story.
tip: 'Contar' means to count AND to tell. 'Nos contó una historia' = he told us a story. English hides the same link inside 'recount.'

target: Lo encontré en el autobús.
english: I found it on the bus.
tip: 'Lo encontré' = 'it I-found.' Object pronouns jump BEFORE the verb in Spanish – you say the 'what' before the action, the reverse of English.

target: Vivimos en un departamento pequeño.
english: We live in a small apartment.
tip: Piso = apartment (Spain). In Latin America: departamento or apartamento.

target: Cenamos juntos en la cocina.
english: We have dinner together in the kitchen.
tip: There's no 'we' here – the -amos in cenamos does that job alone. Adding nosotros would add emphasis, like saying 'WE dine together, unlike some people'.

target: El concierto es a las nueve.
english: The concert is at nine.
tip: Ser for scheduled events: "La reunión es a las 3." Use ser for when/where events happen.

target: Nos llamamos por teléfono cada semana.
english: We call each other every week.
tip: "Llamarse" can be reciprocal: "Nos llamamos" = We call each other. Also reflexive: "Me llamo Ana" = I'm called Ana.

target: El cliente no contestó mi llamada.
english: The client didn't answer my call.
tip: 'Contestó' isn't 'contested'! Contestar just means to answer – no argument implied. 'No contestó mi llamada' = he didn't answer my call.

target: Mi abuela nos visitó el domingo.
english: My grandmother visited us on Sunday.
tip: No 'on' needed: 'el domingo' alone means ON Sunday. The article el does the job English gives a preposition – nos visitó el domingo.

target: Fui al mercado por mi madre.
english: I went to the market for my mother.
tip: 'Fui al mercado por mi madre' is ambiguous on purpose: for her sake, in her place, or even to fetch her. Por bundles motive – English 'for' can't tell you which; context does.

target: Se cayó la taza y se rompió.
english: The cup fell and broke.
tip: The se makes it nobody's fault: se cayó, se rompió – the cup fell and broke all by itself. Spanish loves this no-blame se: things just happen, no culprit named.

target: Mi padre se jubiló el año pasado.
english: My father retired last year.
tip: 'Se jubiló' comes from júbilo – jubilation. Spanish literally frames retiring as bursting into joy: my father 'joyed himself' out of work.

target: Me va bien quedar a las seis.
english: Meeting at six works for me.
tip: 'Quedar' here means to arrange to MEET, not to stay. 'Quedar a las seis' = let's meet at six – the all-purpose verb for making plans with friends.

target: Hace dos meses que no la veo.
english: I haven't seen her for two months.
tip: Literally 'it makes two months that I don't see her' – present-tense veo, no perfect needed, because the not-seeing is still true at this very moment.

target: Hace tres meses que empecé este curso.
english: I started this course three months ago.
tip: 'Hace tres meses que empecé' = 'it MAKES three months that I started.' Spanish turns 'ago' into the verb hacer – hace + time up front, que hooks on the event.

target: Mi padre siempre quiso que fuéramos a la universidad.
english: My father always wanted us to go to university.
tip: You can't 'want someone TO do' in Spanish. When the subjects differ it's que + subjunctive: 'quiso que fuéramos' = he wanted that we-went.

target: El motivo por el cual no vine fue una emergencia familiar.
english: The reason I didn't come was a family emergency.
tip: Por el cual = for which, more formal than por el que.

target: Salgo para Madrid a las siete.
english: I leave for Madrid at seven.
tip: Para + destination = heading toward.

target: Mi hija pintó un cuadro precioso.
english: My daughter painted a beautiful picture.
tip: 'Precioso' rarely means precious – it's the everyday word for gorgeous. 'Un cuadro precioso' = a beautiful painting, no gemstones involved.

target: Mi hermana me prestó su carro.
english: My sister lent me her car.
tip: Spanish has no verb 'to borrow' – only 'prestar' (lend). Borrowing is pedir prestado, 'asking lent.' 'Me prestó su carro' = she lent me her car.

target: El jefe nos invitó a comer.
english: The boss invited us to lunch.
tip: When someone says 'nos invitó a comer,' they're paying! Invitar means invite AND treat – accept the invitation and your wallet stays shut.

target: Llegué tarde por culpa del tráfico.
english: I arrived late because of traffic.
tip: Por culpa de = because of (blaming). Llegué = I arrived.

target: Salud, que tengas un día maravilloso!
english: Cheers, have a wonderful day!
tip: No 'I hope' needed: Spanish launches wishes with bare que + subjunctive. "Que tengas un día maravilloso" = (may) you have – the espero stays silent.

target: Cuando era niño, vivía cerca del mar.
english: When I was a child, I lived near the sea.
tip: Both imperfect: era + vivía. Habitual past – describes how things used to be.

target: Ella se pintó las uñas de rojo.
english: She painted her nails red.
tip: 'Se pintó LAS uñas' – the nails, not 'her' nails. With body parts, the reflexive se already says whose, so Spanish skips the possessive.

target: Desafortunadamente no puedo asistir a la reunión.
english: Unfortunately I can't attend the meeting.
tip: 'Asistir' doesn't mean assist – it means ATTEND. 'Asistir a la reunión' = go to the meeting. To help someone is ayudar.
